learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to technically correctly, completely, and manufacturing-appropriately represent individual components and assemblies.
Students learn the confident use of CAD functions and methods to create 3D models of components and assemblies for subsequent product development processes.

Through targeted practice tasks, students acquire basic knowledge for dimensioning manufactured parts and recognize their influence on various manufacturing processes, such as drilling, bending, turning, and milling.
Students are able to grasp and understand a task within a given subject area, and develop suitable solutions for its implementation.
Students are able to critically evaluate these solution approaches based on the experiences gained.
Students are able to present the results structured in writing and orally.

syllabus_topics: Specifications for surface roughness, hardness, and form and position tolerances
Preparing a complete bill of materials
Fundamentals of working with PTC Creo
Solving a small development task creatively
Practical implementation using various manufacturing processes (milling, turning, 3D printing)
Application of modern technologies (e.g., Internet of Things (IoT), Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR))

assessment_methods.method: Exam tasks at the CAD workstation

assessment_rules: All examination performances (MABB151, MABB152, MABB153) are ungraded. Participation in all lectures and laboratory sessions for MABB152 is mandatory. Exercises completed during MABB152 count as a pre-exam requirement.
